$comment: What a human has actually verified, and at which release. Written by
read by that script and by `scripts/check-manual-test-roster.mjs`.
THIS FILE IS THE RECORD. There is no per-release run document, deliberately:
a document with ticks on it would be a second copy of the roster, which is the
exact drift the guard beside it exists to stop. One stamp per entry, and the
history is git log, which answers 'what did we verify at v0.5, and did the
thing that failed there pass here' by reading a diff rather than by hunting
for last release's file. Day-of ticking still happens in the release issue,
An entry is as verified as its WORST row: one failed observation on one client
records `fail` for the entry, whatever its siblings did.
`verdict: override` is how a failed ship gate gets passed anyway. It carries a
written reason, the guard refuses one shorter than 40 characters, and it lands
in git under the name of whoever committed it. That is the whole mechanism:
the default is to stop, and going on is a named act rather than a silence.
Empty on purpose. Nothing has been verified under this roster yet, and the
guard says so out loud on every run rather than letting an absent file read as
